script: I helped break the Nazi codes, and I couldn't tell my wife for thirty years. In 1942, I was recruited to Bletchley Park under the Official Secrets Act, and sworn never to speak a word of it, to anyone, for the rest of my life. My own wife thought I spent the war filing paperwork in some forgotten office. She married a man she believed did nothing important at all. Every single day, I broke ciphers that saved thousands of lives, and every single night, I came home and said nothing. In 1974, the government finally lifted the secrecy, and a book revealed what Bletchley Park had really done. My wife read it before I ever said a word. She looked at me and asked if it was true. I helped break the Nazi codes, and my own wife found out from a book.

description:
Bletchley Park codebreakers were sworn to total silence under the Official Secrets Act. Many, like this veteran, couldn't tell their own spouses what they did in the war until the government declassified it in 1974.

Could you keep a secret like that from your own family? Let me know in the comments.
